title: Shaw levels Madrid as City's women draw 1-1 in Champions League, October 1
dek: Manchester City's women's team drew 1-1 with Real Madrid on October 1, 2026, in the Women's Champions League league stage. Khadija Shaw scored City's second-half equalizer after Linda Caicedo gave Madrid the lead. The result leaves both teams with two points from their opening two fixtures.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Khadija Shaw scored Manchester City's equalizer in the second half to draw 1-1 with Real Madrid in the Women's Champions League on October 1, 2026.
bottom_line: City remain in contention for knockout qualification but sit behind Barcelona and level with Madrid and their other remaining opponents. Group-stage play continues into November; a second loss or continued draws could push City toward the playoff bracket for the best third-place finishers.
body:
Manchester City's women's team drew 1-1 with Real Madrid on October 1, 2026, in the Women's Champions League league stage, holding level after Real Madrid opened the scoring in the first half.
Khadija Shaw scored City's equalizer in the second half, per Guardian Sport reporting. Shaw's goal was her fifth of the season in all competitions and her first of the Champions League campaign.
Linear Madrid's Linda Caicedo scored first with a low finish into the bottom corner.
City made substitutions bringing on Beth Mead, Sam Coffey, and Grace Clinton from the bench, which appeared to strengthen the hosts. The match was described as high-quality and a fair reflection of an even but entertaining game, per Guardian Sport.
After two fixtures, both City and Madrid held two points. City's earlier opening fixture was a draw at Bayern Munich. Barcelona are the only WCL team with six points after two games, having thrashed Roma on Wednesday, per Guardian Sport. Inter drew 1-1 with Austria Vienna, with Ivana Andrés leveling in the fourth minute of added time. PSG defeated Leuven 5-0. HB Køge defeated Servette 5-1 in Denmark.
Head coach Andree Jeglertz said the noise surrounding the men's club's guilty verdict had zero impact on the women's team. "Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm, I haven't seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players' performance," Jeglertz said, per Guardian Sport. On the draw itself, he stated: "It is OK, it's an OK start in the Champions League. It's not ideal but it's a good start and we know what is needed from us in the rest of the tournament."
